injuries.description: degloving injury of the right foot. Debridement and split thickness skin graft was done.
source: the plaintiff suffered a degloving injury of the right foot. Debridement and split thickness skin graft was done.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified open wound of ankle or foot

injuries.description: The normal pad of soft tissue is absent and the undersurface of the calcaneus is only covered by a layer of inefficient skin.
injuries.body_part: right heel / undersurface of the calcaneus
source: The problem today is the situation under the heel. The normal pad of soft tissue is absent and the undersurface of the calcaneus is only covered by a layer of inefficient skin.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

injuries.description: 8" x 6" flat scar on the right thigh, this being the donor site for skin grafts.
source: there is a 8" x 6" flat scar on the right thigh, this being the donor site for skin grafts.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the hip or thigh

manifestations.description: If the plaintiff walks any distance the skin breaks down, and indeed, Mr Wedderburn observed obvious healing areas.
Some restriction of movement of the left ankle but this is due to his spastic situation.
On the right inversion is 10° and eversion is non-existent.
He has also lost 50% of the movement of his right toes.
Considering the matter overall Mr Wedderburn considered there was a 12% impairment of the leg which gave a 5% impairment of the whole man.

treatments_received: follow-up at South Kwai Chung Clinic

losses.description: the effect of this plaintiff's disability meant there was a no longer reasonable mobility and there was a general marring of the general activities and enjoyment of life.
scarring and impairment of the right foot and donor site scarring on the right thigh with resulting functional impairment.

As a result of the accident he has lost the source of income. "Although the impairment is relatively slight, it resulted in him losing his work, and such a man could only perform very simple forms of work of the type he was doing."
